Subject: Nimbus POC traffic intake & evaluation plan — post-call decisions

Alex / Priya (cc'd),

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for the time. Below is a concise recap of what we agreed on and the concrete next steps so we can scope the POC and get a trial scheduled. If anything below is off, reply with the correction and we'll update the plan.

POC objective (agreed):
- Validate Redwood inference performance and cost for Nimbus Health's real-time charting assistant (latency <= 250ms p95 for interactive calls, no more than 35% cost increase vs current serving baseline).
- Verify behavioral fidelity on your prompt sets (privacy-preserving evals) and stability during morning/afternoon bursts.

Success criteria (what Nimbus will sign off on):
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for 75% of test queries during steady-state RPS.
- Throughput: sustain 150 RPS steady-state with 20 concurrent users and absorb bursts to 750 RPS for up to 90s without error rate > 1%.
- Token profile: avg request payload ~340 tokens, avg response ~120 tokens; 95th percentile response length ~900 tokens (for summarization tasks).
- Quality: no more than 5% degradation on your regression prompt set (we'll run 200 labeled prompts).
- Cost: expected per-1M token cost delta within the pilot tolerance you set (you said ~+20% acceptable).

Traffic intake asks (what we need from Nimbus):
1) Representative sample traffic file (anonymized JSONL) with 1,000 requests showing: endpoint name, sequence length (input tokens), expected output length, concurrency hints, and a timestamp field for burst modeling — deliver by Tue, Oct 26.
2) Peak windows: typical morning burst 08:30–09:15 ET, secondary peak 16:45–17:10 ET. Confirm sizes if different.
3) Auth / endpoint details for integration (API key + URL we can hit from our staging subnet) — if you'd rather not expose keys, we can replay sample traffic on our side.

Redwood deliverables and owners: (target dates)
- Ingest + traffic replay & baseline run (Jordan): start Oct 28, results by Oct 30.
- Canary config and cost projection (Soojin): Canary plan + cost delta by Oct 29.
- Throughput tuning + kernel selection probe (Ben): preliminary probe by Oct 29, full run by Nov 1.

Attachments & links:
- Attached: Nimbus POC template (nimbus-poc-template.xlsx) — please populate traffic filename + any redlines to success criteria.
- HubSpot deal link: https://hubspot.company.com/deal/12345
- Shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cNimbusPOC

Immediate next steps (actions):
- Alex / Priya: provide anonymized sample traffic and confirm peak windows by Tue, Oct 26.
- Jordan / Ben / Soojin: prepare the replay environment and an initial canary config; share a short readout on Oct 30.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

Jordan Blake

Quick update after a short sandbox probe I spun up: 
- Baseline results (short replay, synthetic): 150 RPS steady -> p95 ~220ms on a 8xA100 config with our medium quantized runtime. Error rate 0.3% during steady.
- Burst probe (ramped to 750 RPS for 60s): p95 moves to ~480ms, error rate 1.4% (exceeded target). Causes look like KV cache misses + insufficient batching window under high concurrency.

Questions / blockers for Nimbus: 
1) For long-note requests (>700 tokens) do you want us to route those to a larger-context variant or serve from same model? If you prefer separate routing we can add a policy rule to offload >1k token responses to a larger instance.
2) Are there any regulatory gating windows where we cannot replay traffic from our staging IPs?

I've attached the POC template (nimbus-poc-template.xlsx) with the probe notes filled in. Next steps:
- I'll iterate on kernel tuning to improve burst behavior; plan to test different batch windows and a modest KV-prefetch change.
- Soojin, once you have the cost numbers we can propose a canary traffic split to keep bursts under an SLO during initial ramp.

Ben
